_comment: Macro benchmark baseline: bots replaying the standard session.
Regenerate: bot bench --rounds 120 --json benches/macro-baseline.json
Gate: CI fails if p99 exceeds 2x this value (bot::bench::REGRESSION_FACTOR).
The workload fields are checked, not decorative: comparing a run at a
different --rounds measures the parameters rather than the server.
HARDWARE MATTERS. These came from the machine named below; a CI runner is
different silicon and will not reproduce them exactly. The 2x threshold
absorbs that, which is also why it cannot be tightened without a
dedicated benchmark machine.
REBASELINED 2026-08-04 because the WORKLOAD changed, not because the
server got slower. The benchmark used to run with no mods, so its world
was pure air. That was harmless while nothing moved, and turned
pathological the moment Task 09 gave players physics: every bot
free-falls for ever, its interest set follows it down, and the server
generates and encodes a fresh layer of chunks every tick for the whole
run. Nightly caught it as a p99 that had doubled. It now runs on the
reference generator's ground, which is what a real server does.
Attribution was measured rather than assumed, by running with and
without the player step: in a world with ground the physics costs
nothing on the mean and sits inside the run-to-run noise on p99, which
matches Task 02b's 0.0136 ms/tick for a hundred bodies. In the air world
it doubled p99 — all of it chunk generation chasing bodies that were
never going to land.
_machine: dev container, AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, release build
